evidence: Single package ('sgd') with multiple modules, indicating tight integration without service boundaries
Clear module separation by concern (cache, gdrive, meta, ptn, routes, streams, utils) with low coupling
Routes module imports domain modules (gdrive, meta, streams) but does not act as a strict controller (no MVC separation of view)
No evidence of service communication, messaging, or deployment boundaries
Flask used as monolithic web framework with route handlers co-located with domain logic
All code resides in a single Python package with 2-level directory depth, typical of a modular monolith
risks: Risk of tight coupling over time due to mutual imports between modules (e.g., utils imports from cache, routes imports from multiple modules)
Monolithic scaling limitations for high-traffic scenarios
Testing may require complex mocking of interdependent modules
